completed_tasks.name: readonly-slave shared-buffer experiment for dual-engine combing
completed_tasks.outcome: Sounded bad (crackling, instant engine character changed). Reverted before commit. Confirmed shared work_buf with snap-register reader can't avoid corrupting the reader's reflection computation.

completed_tasks.name: collapse to single SPU engine; rename engineBlend -> morphSpeed
strip granular haze + freeze layer (failed experiment)
completed_tasks.rationale: Granular texture sat audibly separate from reverb tail; APF diffusion + LP matching couldn't integrate it.

completed_tasks.name: spu94_set_slew_duration() C-core API + cubic ease-out slew
Morph Speed knob moved into MorphPanel (PS1 mauve, bottom of viewport)
A/B-tested slew curves: linear, smoothstep, cubic, quartic, quintic, true exponential, vIIR three-phase hold
completed_tasks.outcome: All 7 variants A/B-indistinguishable in audio; trajectories verified via diagnostic to match their designs. Audible bottleneck is downstream of slew (reverb network integration time).

completed_tasks.name: Clean up: removed slew_inc dead field, three-phase vIIR branch, diagnostic tool

remaining_tasks.name: Optional: cherry-pick b65b8a2 (Phase 18 crackle fix from master)

Open creative direction: attack morph character at audio level instead of register level (filter sweep / wet duck / dry-wet ramp during morph)

decisions.rationale: Two coherent reverbs summed = combing. Decorrelating the inputs defeats the morph idea. Three-engine architecture was an exploration scaffold, not a production pattern. engines[1] kept as silent scratch for morph register snapshots.
Texture is fundamentally a separate signal from reverb tail; can't integrate without losing the granular character that motivated it. APF + LP attempts only made it darker, not 'one with' the reverb.

decisions.decision: Cubic ease-out slew, all registers same curve
decisions.rationale: Empirically confirmed via diagnostic that 7 different curve shapes / per-register schedules produce A/B-indistinguishable audio. Reverb network's own integration time dominates. Cubic kept as simplest non-linear option.

decisions.decision: Morph Speed knob in MorphPanel viewport, not bottom margin
decisions.rationale: Originally in bottom margin (40px); moved to MorphPanel at bottom of viewport (60px, PS1 mauve palette) for visual prominence near the morph encoder. Visually separate from mixer/DAC bar.

next_action: Decide whether to bring forward functional pieces from master (crackle fix at b65b8a2, Error Accumulator at Phase 19), or attack morph character at the audio level (filter sweep / wet duck / dry-wet ramp during morph) instead of register level. The slew machinery is now stable and proven correct — further perceptual gains on morph feel will require working outside the SPU register path.

anti_patterns_discovered_this_session.pattern: Sum two coherent reverbs, then try to fix the comb with shared memory or readonly slaves
anti_patterns_discovered_this_session.mitigation: The math doesn't allow it. Two near-identical reverbs on identical input ARE a comb filter. Decorrelating inputs (different EQ, predelay) defeats the morph idea. If layered character is wanted, must accept the comb as a sound; if clean morph is wanted, must use one engine.

anti_patterns_discovered_this_session.pattern: Iterate on slew curve shape without first verifying the curve change actually produces a different register trajectory
anti_patterns_discovered_this_session.mitigation: Write a diagnostic (like tools/slew_trace.c was) before tuning curves. Confirm the C core is doing what you think it is. We wasted 7 variant cycles before measuring.

context_notes: Substantial cleanup session. Started by reverting the readonly-slave dual-engine experiment (sounded bad). Then collapsed three-engine architecture to one, stripped haze/freeze granular layer, renamed engineBlend -> morphSpeed, moved the knob into MorphPanel with PS1 styling, added spu94_set_slew_duration() C-core API. Then went down a 7-variant rabbit hole on slew curve shape — all sounded the same. Diagnostic confirmed all curves produced their designed register trajectories; lesson is that at slew durations <500ms, register-level curve choice is below audible threshold and the reverb network's own integration time dominates. Cleaned up dead code from the rabbit hole. Net session diff: -106 lines, mostly from granular cleanup. Plugin running PID 91900 with the final cubic build.
